description: CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became. LS-DATE='          ' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYY-MM-DD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85); LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. This program opens no file and is reached by no JCL, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and takes no job parameter - its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57 and the group move at L122, never captured from a COBOL run, which is impossible here. Arm 8 with a BLANK date against a well-formed mask - the empty-input path. It matters because blanks are tolerated at the edges of a numeric field, so a validator could plausibly have treated an all-blank date as an omitted value and defaulted it; here it supplies no digit at all and is refused. The L122 group move then reports eight blanks in WS-DATE behind the two halfword bytes, which is itself worth pinning: the message is 80 bytes wide whatever the input was.
